findings.title: New "refuse the land intent when targets are unverifiable" rule lands in a log-only catch — no operation, no held state, no escalation, no reclose door
findings.detail:
New in round 3. §2.5 line 79 adds: "`StateStore.ensureLandOperation` 创建 intent 前，provider …验证全部目标；…缺必需来源拒绝新 intent，不能先创建再异步补." It never says where that refusal is recorded or how it escalates — and the only thing `ensureLandOperation` can do today is throw (`invalid_land_operation` / `land_operation_run_conflict` / `land_operation_not_created`, StateStore.ts:71691-71740).

On the automated engine path that throw is swallowed. `store.ensureLandOperation(...)` is called at workflow-engine-dispatcher.ts:2269, inside `private async consume(intent)` (line 2184). Its only caller is line 415 `const started = await this.consume(intent);`, whose catch at lines 418-425 does `result.held += 1; this.log(...)` — a counter and a log line. No `holdWorkflowLandNode`, no `alertIdentity`, no persisted state. The reconcile loop re-enters on the next pass and logs again, forever.

Because no `land_operation` row is created, every recovery mechanism this plan builds is unreachable: §5's escalation outbox is keyed on `(operationId, resumeGeneration, retryEpoch, held)`; the `closeout_only` reclose door is `POST /api/lifecycle/land/:operationId/resume` and has no operationId to address; and the 8-retry→held budget (land-retry-policy.ts:61-63,124-131) never starts. That is a new silently-stuck shape on the main landing path for every future land, strictly worse than today where an intent is always created and failures enter the retry/held/escalation machinery. It also contradicts §1 invariant 5 ("第九次耗尽仍可 held，但事务性登记 Lead escalation") and §5 ("…不能丢掉工单"), and it repeats the exact anti-pattern research.md already flags at land-executor.ts:1855-1883 ("held notification 失败只 log … 不能仅依赖 best-effort").

Note the asymmetry that makes this clearly an oversight rather than a choice: the legacy branch at line 80 *does* specify escalation ("返回 `worktree_target_unresolved` 并输出具体待补证项和正式 reclose 门"), and it works only because an operation already exists. The new-operation branch has none.

Required: specify that the refusal is a structured result, not a bare throw, and name its destination — for the engine path, `holdLandRun(reason)` → `store.holdWorkflowLandNode({..., alertIdentity})` (workflow-engine-dispatcher.ts:2196-2215), which is the existing alert-bearing hold; for the operator path (`createIntent` at plugin.ts:8494 and 8537) a typed refusal surfaced as the lifecycle route's 409. Give the reason string, and add a §6 A test asserting the refusal produces a persisted alert-bearing hold rather than a log line.
findings.failure_scenario: A DAG run reaches its land node while one attributed worktree's `git worktree list` probe is unreadable (EACCES, or the repo lock is held long enough to time out), so target verification is incomplete. `ensureLandOperation` refuses; the throw is caught at workflow-engine-dispatcher.ts:418; the dispatcher logs `workflow engine dispatch held for <execId>: …` and returns. No land_operation exists, so no held row, no outbox escalation, no thread notification, and no `/land/:operationId/resume` target. The approved, merged PR's issue never closes out and nothing tells the Lead — the reconcile loop just re-logs every pass.

findings.title: The mandatory target snapshot cannot be written by `ensureLandOperation` as specified: it is synchronous, `INSERT OR IGNORE`, and the legacy backfill trigger misses pre-migration operations that land normally
findings.detail:
New in round 3. §2.5 line 79 requires "完整 JSON 与 digest 在 intent transaction 一并落库", but `ensureLandOperation` (StateStore.ts:71691-71760) is a synchronous better-sqlite3 `this.db.transaction(() => …)` taking only `{runId?, issueId, projectName, prNumber, approvedHead, now}`. Two of the three sources the plan requires are async: `WorktreeManager.getRegisteredWorktree` spawns `git worktree list` and `readWorktreeGeneration` reads the marker file — neither can be awaited inside that transaction. The plan should state the interface change explicitly (the verified targets payload + digest becomes a parameter, produced by the provider under the issue+repo lock, and the transaction writes it atomically), because "创建 intent 前…验证" reads as verify-then-create and leaves the ordering to the implementer. The safety consequence is already defused by "snapshot 只证明原目标身份，不代替删除时的现状/分支/generation/进程检查", which is why this is not blocking.

Two related gaps in the same paragraph:
(a) `ensureLandOperation` is `INSERT OR IGNORE` and returns the pre-existing row on re-entry (StateStore.ts:71716-71735). If targets are written only on insert, a second `ensureLandOperation` for the same `(project, issue, pr, head)` silently leaves whatever is there — including NULL. State that an existing row with NULL/stale `closeout_targets_version` must enter the backfill branch rather than be treated as captured.
(b) The legacy backfill trigger at line 80 is "首个 closeout-only claim" — but `closeout_only` is the §5 operator reclose mode. An operation created before the migration that then lands through the ordinary path never takes a closeout-only claim, so its targets stay NULL with no stated capture point. Widen the trigger to the first claim that reaches closeout (ordinary or reclose), which is also the last moment sessions are still present.
findings.failure_scenario: A land operation row already exists from before the migration (created by an earlier `ensureLandOperation` call). The Bridge is upgraded; the operation resumes and lands through the normal engine path, never taking a closeout-only claim. `closeout_targets_json` stays NULL, no backfill runs while the sessions are still present, and by the time closeout needs the targets the surviving bindings may already be gone — reproducing the very `worktree_target_unresolved` state the round-2 fix was written to prevent.
